# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 54 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 54 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_054_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 5, Introduction — What Is a True Fast?

**54:1** As I was fasting and sitting on a certain mountain and giving thanks to the Lord for all the things he had done for me, I saw the Shepherd sitting beside me, saying: "Why have you come here so early in the morning?" "Because, lord," I replied, "I have a station to observe." "What is this station?" he asked. "I am keeping a fast, lord," I said. "What is this fast that you are keeping?" he asked.

**54:2** "As I have been accustomed, lord," I said. "You do not know," he said, "how to fast to the Lord. This empty fast that you observe before him is not a fast." "Why so, lord?" I asked. "I tell you," he said, "that this fast you suppose to be a fast is not a fast. But I will teach you what a fast is that is complete and acceptable to the Lord.

**54:3** Hear," he said. "God does not desire such an empty fast. For by fasting in this manner before God, you accomplish nothing righteous. But fast to God with a fast of this kind: do no evil in your life, and serve the Lord with a pure heart; keep his commandments, walking in his ordinances, and let no evil desire arise in your heart; trust in God. If you do these things and fear him and abstain from every evil deed, you shall live to God. And if you do these things, you shall accomplish a great fast and one truly acceptable to God."

---

*LOGOS renders according to the Greek text of P.Mich. 130 with attention to formal correspondence and the prophetic redefinition of fasting in Similitude 5.*
